question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution was added to prevent defection of elected members? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Ninth Schedule
Eleventh Schedule
Tenth Schedule
Eighth Schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tenth Schedule

Explanation:
The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, also known as the 'Anti-defection Law', was added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985. Its purpose is to prevent elected members from switching parties. If a member voluntarily gives up party membership or votes against the party whip, they can be disqualified from the House. The schedule applies to both Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. It was further strengthened by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003. The presiding officer (Speaker/Chairman) is the authority to decide disqualification cases. This law has enhanced political stability and party discipline in India.

☛ Tenth Schedule is related to? → Anti-defection
☛ Which amendment added Tenth Schedule? → 52nd Amendment
☛ When was the anti-defection law amended? → 2003 (91st Amendment)
☛ Who decides disqualification under Tenth Schedule? → Presiding officer
☛ Which houses are covered by Tenth Schedule? → Lok Sabha and assemblies
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के किस अनुसूची को निर्वाचित सदस्यों के दल-बदल को रोकने के लिए जोड़ा गया था? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: नवमीं अनुसूची
ग्यारहवीं अनुसूची
दसवीं अनुसूची
आठवीं अनुसूची
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है दसवीं अनुसूची

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की दसवीं अनुसूची को 52वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1985 द्वारा जोड़ा गया, जिसे 'दल-बदल विरोधी कानून' कहा जाता है। इसका उद्देश्य निर्वाचित सदस्यों द्वारा एक पार्टी से दूसरी पार्टी में जाने को रोकना था। यदि कोई सदस्य स्वेच्छा से अपनी पार्टी की सदस्यता छोड़ता है या पार्टी के व्हिप के विरुद्ध मतदान करता है, तो उसे सदन की सदस्यता से अयोग्य ठहराया जा सकता है। इस अनुसूची को 91वें संशोधन, 2003 द्वारा और मजबूत किया गया। दसवीं अनुसूची लोकसभा और राज्य विधानसभाओं दोनों पर लागू होती है। इस कानून ने राजनीतिक स्थिरता बढ़ाने और पार्टी अनुशासन सुनिश्चित करने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई है।

question: When a Judge of a High Court in India, including the Chief Justice, wishes to resign from office, to whom must they submit their resignation? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: The President of India
The Chief Justice of India
The Prime Minister of India
The Governor of the respective state
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The President of India

Explanation:
According to Article 217(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution, a Judge of a High Court (including the Chief Justice) must submit their resignation to the President of India. The President accepts the resignation, after which the position becomes vacant. This provision ensures the independence of High Court judges. The same procedure is followed for Supreme Court judges under Article 124. Neither the Governor nor the Chief Justice of India has the constitutional authority to accept such resignations. The rule that resignations are addressed to the President reflects the central control over the judiciary.

☛ To whom does a Supreme Court judge submit resignation? → President of India
☛ Who appoints High Court judges? → President of India
☛ Who appoints the Chief Justice of a High Court? → President of India
☛ Who administers oath to a High Court judge? → Governor of the state
question_hi: भारत में उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश, जिसमें मुख्य न्यायाधीश भी शामिल हैं, यदि वे अपने पद से त्यागपत्र देना चाहते हैं, तो उन्हें किसे अपना त्यागपत्र प्रस्तुत करना होगा? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: भारत के राष्ट्रपति
भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश
भारत के प्रधानमंत्री
संबंधित राज्य के राज्यपाल
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत के राष्ट्रपति

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 217(1)(a) के अनुसार, किसी उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश (मुख्य न्यायाधीश सहित) का त्यागपत्र राष्ट्रपति को संबोधित किया जाना चाहिए। राष्ट्रपति त्यागपत्र स्वीकार करते हैं, जिसके बाद पद रिक्त हो जाता है। यह प्रावधान उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीशों की स्वतंत्रता सुनिश्चित करता है। अनुच्छेद 124 में उच्चतम न्यायालय के न्यायाधीशों के लिए भी यही प्रक्रिया है। राज्यपाल या मुख्य न्यायाधीश को त्यागपत्र देने का प्रावधान संवैधानिक रूप से सही नहीं है। राष्ट्रपति को त्यागपत्र देने का नियम न्यायपालिका की केंद्रीय नियंत्रण में होने का प्रतीक है।

question: Which of the following is a constitutional body? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: NITI Aayog
Election Commission of India
National Human Rights Commission
State Human Rights Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Election Commission of India

Explanation:
The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Constitution. It is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in the country. NITI Aayog is a non-constitutional body, created by an executive order. The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) are statutory bodies established by acts of Parliament. Therefore, only the Election Commission of India is a constitutional body directly set up by the Constitution.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which article establishes the Election Commission? → Article 324
☛ NITI Aayog is which type of body? → Non-constitutional / executive body
☛ Which act created NHRC? → Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
☛ Examples of constitutional bodies → Election Commission, UPSC, CAG, Finance Commission
☛ Which body is not directly established by the Constitution? → NHRC (statutory body)
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा एक संवैधानिक निकाय है? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: नीति आयोग
भारत निर्वाचन आयोग
राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार आयोग
राज्य मानवाधिकार आयोग
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत निर्वाचन आयोग

Explanation:
भारत निर्वाचन आयोग एक संवैधानिक निकाय है, जिसका गठन अनुच्छेद 324 के तहत किया गया है। यह देश में स्वतंत्र और निष्पक्ष चुनाव सुनिश्चित करने के लिए जिम्मेदार है। नीति आयोग एक गैर-संवैधानिक निकाय है, जिसे कार्यपालिका आदेश द्वारा स्थापित किया गया। राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार आयोग (NHRC) और राज्य मानवाधिकार आयोग (SHRC) वैधानिक निकाय हैं, जो संसद द्वारा पारित अधिनियम के तहत बनाए गए हैं। इस प्रकार, केवल भारत निर्वाचन आयोग ही संविधान द्वारा सीधे स्थापित संवैधानिक निकाय है।

question: Separation of executive from judiciary is contained in which of the following? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Preamble
Fundamental Duties
Fundamental Rights
Directive Principles of State Policy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Directive Principles of State Policy

Explanation:
The provision for separation of the executive from the judiciary is contained in Article 50 under Part IV of the Indian Constitution, which deals with Directive Principles of State Policy. This Article directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services. It is a key principle ensuring judicial independence, though it is non-justiciable. The Directive Principles serve as guidelines for the government while framing policies. Among the options, the Preamble outlines the objectives of the Constitution, Fundamental Duties (Part IVA) list civic duties, and Fundamental Rights (Part III) guarantee individual liberties. Therefore, the correct answer is Directive Principles of State Policy.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article related to separation of executive and judiciary → Article 50
☛ Part containing Article 50 → Part IV (Directive Principles)
☛ Nature of Article 50 → Non-justiciable
☛ Key principle behind this provision → Separation of powers
☛ Part of Constitution dealing with Directive Principles → Part IV
question_hi: कार्यपालिका को न्यायपालिका से पृथक्करण निम्नलिखित में से किसमें निहित है? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)

मौलिक कर्तव्य
मौलिक अधिकार
राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में अनुच्छेद 50 राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों के अंतर्गत कार्यपालिका को न्यायपालिका से पृथक्करण का प्रावधान करता है। यह एक नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांत है, जो सरकार को नीतियाँ बनाने में मार्गदर्शन करता है। यह अनुच्छेद राज्य को यह निर्देश देता है कि वह सार्वजनिक सेवाओं में न्यायपालिका को कार्यपालिका से अलग करने के लिए कदम उठाए। यह न्यायिक स्वतंत्रता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है। हालाँकि यह प्रावधान न्यायोचित नहीं है, फिर भी यह शासन के लिए मौलिक माना जाता है। अन्य विकल्पों में प्रस्तावना संविधान के उद्देश्यों को बताती है, मौलिक कर्तव्य नागरिकों के कर्तव्य हैं, और मौलिक अधिकार नागरिकों को सुरक्षा प्रदान करते हैं।

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India says that all public places are open to all citizens? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 30
Article 21
Article 15(2)
Article 16(2)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 15(2)

Explanation:
Article 15 of the Indian Constitution prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. Its clause (2) specifically states that no citizen shall be denied access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, places of public entertainment, or the use of wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads and places of public resort maintained by the state or dedicated to public use, solely on these grounds. This provision is part of the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18) and ensures equal access to public spaces for all citizens. Article 30 deals with minority educational institutions, Article 21 with right to life and personal liberty, and Article 16(2) with equality of opportunity in public employment.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article guaranteeing equal access to public places → Article 15(2)
☛ Forbidden grounds under Article 15 → Religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth
☛ Public places covered under Article 15(2) → Shops, restaurants, hotels, entertainment venues, wells, tanks, roads
☛ Part containing Article 15 → Part III (Fundamental Rights)
☛ Articles related to Right to Equality → 14 to 18
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का कौन सा अनुच्छेद कहता है कि सभी सार्वजनिक स्थान सभी नागरिकों के लिए खुले हैं? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 30
अनुच्छेद 21
अनुच्छेद 15(2)
अनुच्छेद 16(2)
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 15(2)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 15 धर्म, मूलवंश, जाति, लिंग या जन्म स्थान के आधार पर भेदभाव पर रोक लगाता है। इसके खंड (2) के अनुसार, कोई भी नागरिक केवल धर्म, मूलवंश, जाति, लिंग या जन्म स्थान के कारण दुकानों, सार्वजनिक रेस्तरां, होटलों, सार्वजनिक मनोरंजन स्थलों या सार्वजनिक कुओं, तालाबों, स्नानघाटों, सड़कों के उपयोग से वंचित नहीं किया जाएगा। यह प्रावधान समानता के अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 14-18) का हिस्सा है और सार्वजनिक स्थानों तक सभी नागरिकों की समान पहुंच सुनिश्चित करता है। अनुच्छेद 30 अल्पसंख्यकों के शैक्षणिक संस्थानों से, अनुच्छेद 21 जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता से, और अनुच्छेद 16(2) सार्वजनिक रोजगार में अवसर की समानता से संबंधित है।

question: 'Equal pay for equal work is prevention of concentration of wealth' is mentioned under which Article of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)

Article 44
Article 39
Article 40

question: Which Act abolished the dyarchy in provinces and introduced provincial autonomy during the British rule?  (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Government of India Act, 1935
Government of India Act, 1919
Indian Councils Act, 1909
Indian Independence Act, 1947
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1935

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished the dyarchy in provinces and introduced provincial autonomy. It divided provinces into separate entities and granted them the power of self-government. This Act expanded the powers of provincial legislatures and reduced the role of the Governor. It was a significant step towards establishing a federal structure in British India. Before this, the Government of India Act, 1919 had introduced the dyarchy system, where subjects were divided into reserved and transferred categories. The 1935 Act ended this division and gave full responsibility to provinces, though the federal system at the centre could not be implemented.

question: Which Section of the Citizenship Act, 1955, did the Supreme Court of India uphold in October 2024? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Section 8A
Section 6A
Section 7
Section 6B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Section 6A

Explanation:
The Supreme Court of India in October 2024 upheld Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955, declaring it constitutional. This section was introduced under the Assam Accord of 1985 to grant citizenship to migrants in Assam. The court ruled that Section 6A considers the unique demographic situation of Assam and does not violate fundamental rights. Under Section 6A, migrants who entered Assam before January 1, 1966 can be granted citizenship, while those arriving after March 25, 1971 are to be deported. The judgment brings legal clarity to the citizenship issue in Assam and balances humanitarian concerns with national security.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution provides for the establishment of a Legislative Assembly in a Union Territory? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 241
Article 239
Article 239A
Article 240
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 239A

Explanation:
Part VIII of the Constitution deals with Union Territories. Article 239A provides for the creation of a Legislative Assembly and Council of Ministers for certain Union Territories (currently Delhi and Puducherry). This article was added by the 35th Amendment Act, 1978, which granted a Legislative Assembly to Delhi. Under this article, the Legislative Assembly can make laws on local matters, while the President administers the territory through an Administrator. Article 239 deals with the administration of Union Territories by the President, Article 240 empowers the President to make regulations for some Union Territories, and Article 241 provides for High Courts for Union Territories.

question: Which of the following/who among the following is/are NOT covered under the jurisdiction of the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 1)

Members of the defense forces

solution:

question: Admission and allocation of new states is mentioned in which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 3
Article 4
Article 1
Article 2
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 2

Explanation:
Article 2 of the Indian Constitution deals with the admission or establishment of new states into the Union. It empowers the Parliament to admit new states into the Union of India or establish new states on such terms and conditions as it deems fit. Article 3 pertains to the reorganization of existing states, including changes in boundaries and names. Article 1 defines the name and territory of India, while Article 4 deals with amendments to the First and Fourth Schedules. Thus, the admission and allocation of new states is correctly mentioned under Article 2.

भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 2 संघ में नए राज्यों के प्रवेश या स्थापना से संबंधित है। यह अनुच्छेद संसद को उचित शर्तों पर नए राज्यों को भारतीय संघ में शामिल करने या स्थापित करने का अधिकार देता है। अनुच्छेद 3 राज्यों के पुनर्गठन, सीमा परिवर्तन और नाम परिवर्तन से संबंधित है। अनुच्छेद 1 भारत के नाम और क्षेत्र को परिभाषित करता है जबकि अनुच्छेद 4 संशोधनों की प्रक्रिया से संबंधित है। इस प्रकार, नए राज्यों के प्रवेश का सही उल्लेख अनुच्छेद 2 में है।

question: The State is required to promote the welfare of the people as per which Article of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 39
Article 52
Article 51
Article 38
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 38

Explanation:
Article 38 of the Indian Constitution directs the State to promote the welfare of the people. It is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). According to this article, the State shall strive to maximize the welfare of society by ensuring social, economic, and political justice. It emphasizes reducing inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities. Article 38 is considered the foundation of socialist principles in India. It guides the State to act as a welfare state, though it is not enforceable by courts. The DPSP is borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

question: The States Human Rights Commission is a/an: (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: inter-state body
non-profit organisation
constitutional body
statutory body
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is statutory body

Explanation:
The State Human Rights Commission is a statutory body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It plays a crucial role in enforcing the right to life and personal liberty enshrined in Article 21 of the Constitution. The commission consists of a chairperson and four members, of which two are from a judicial background. Its main objective is to investigate human rights violations and make recommendations to the National Human Rights Commission. A statutory body is created by an act of parliament or state legislature, unlike a constitutional body which is established by the Constitution itself. It is not a non-profit organisation or an inter-state body.

question: Who appoints the Chief Minister of a State? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: The President of India
The Governor of the State
The Speaker of the State Assembly
The Prime Minister of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Governor of the State

Explanation:
According to Article 164 of the Indian Constitution, the Chief Minister of a state is appointed by the Governor. The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and appoints the person who commands a majority in the State Legislative Assembly. This process is based on democratic principles, where after the assembly elections, the Governor invites the leader of the largest party or coalition to form the government and swears them in as Chief Minister. The Chief Minister is the head of the state government and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers. The Governor may exercise discretion in appointing the Chief Minister, especially when there is no clear majority.

question_hi: किसी राज्य के मुख्यमंत्री की नियुक्ति कौन करता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 164 के अनुसार, राज्य के मुख्यमंत्री की नियुक्ति राज्यपाल द्वारा की जाती है। राज्यपाल राज्य का संवैधानिक प्रमुख होता है और वह उस व्यक्ति को मुख्यमंत्री नियुक्त करता है जिसे राज्य विधानसभा में बहुमत का समर्थन प्राप्त हो। यह प्रक्रिया लोकतांत्रिक सिद्धांतों पर आधारित है, जहाँ राज्यपाल विधानसभा चुनावों के बाद सबसे बड़ी पार्टी या गठबंधन के नेता को मुख्यमंत्री पद की शपथ दिलाता है। मुख्यमंत्री राज्य सरकार का प्रमुख होता है और मंत्रिपरिषद की सलाह पर कार्य करता है। राज्यपाल मुख्यमंत्री की नियुक्ति में विवेकाधिकार का प्रयोग कर सकता है, विशेषकर जब स्पष्ट बहुमत न हो।

question: Which of the following Acts established the High Courts at Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Government of India Act, 1858
Indian High Courts Act, 1861
Indian Councils Act, 1909
Charter Act of 1833
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indian High Courts Act, 1861

Explanation:
The Indian High Courts Act, 1861 established the High Courts at Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay. This act abolished the Supreme Courts and Sadar Diwani/Faujdari Adalats and replaced them with High Courts. Each High Court consisted of a Chief Justice and up to 15 judges. This act was a significant step towards unifying the judicial system in India. Prior to this, the Government of India Act, 1858 had transferred the governance of India from the East India Company to the British Crown. The 1861 act strengthened the judiciary and laid the foundation for the High Courts that continue to function today.

भारतीय उच्च न्यायालय अधिनियम, 1861 ने कलकत्ता, मद्रास और बॉम्बे में उच्च न्यायालयों की स्थापना की। इस अधिनियम ने सर्वोच्च न्यायालयों और सदर दीवानी/फौजदारी अदालतों को समाप्त कर उनके स्थान पर उच्च न्यायालय बनाए। प्रत्येक उच्च न्यायालय में एक मुख्य न्यायाधीश और अधिकतम 15 न्यायाधीश होते थे। यह अधिनियम भारत में न्यायिक प्रणाली के एकीकरण की दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम था। इससे पहले, 1858 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम ने भारत का शासन ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी से ब्रिटिश क्राउन को हस्तांतरित किया था। 1861 के इस अधिनियम ने न्यायपालिका को मजबूत किया और उच्च न्यायालयों की नींव रखी जो आज तक कार्यरत हैं।

question: Through which of the following Acts were Indians, for the first time, associated with the executive Councils of the Viceroy and Governors? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Government of India Act, 1935
Government of India Act, 1909
Government of India Act, 1919
Government of India Act, 1929
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1909

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1909 (also known as Morley-Minto Reforms) for the first time associated Indians with the executive councils of the Viceroy and Governors. This act increased the number of Indian members in the legislative councils and provided for the appointment of an Indian member to the Viceroy's executive council. However, this was largely nominal, and real power remained with British officials. The act introduced communal representation by creating separate electorates for Muslims. It marked a significant step in the Indian national movement, laying the groundwork for gradual constitutional reforms.

question: The Regulating Act of 1773 was enacted to regulate which organization’s activities in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 2)

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is East India Company

Explanation:
The Regulating Act of 1773 was passed by the British Parliament to regulate the activities of the East India Company in India. The Company was engaged in both trade and administration, and the Act aimed to bring transparency and establish parliamentary control over its affairs. It was the first major step by the British government to assert authority over the Company's territorial acquisitions and governance in India. The Act also provided for the appointment of a Governor-General of Bengal and a Supreme Court in Calcutta.

question: Which fundamental right has provided Prevention against Arbitrary Arrest and Detention to Indian citizens? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Right to Freedom
Right to Constitutional Remedies
Right Against Exploitation
Right to Equality
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to Freedom

Explanation:
The protection against arbitrary arrest and detention is provided under Article 22 of the Indian Constitution. This article is a part of the Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22). Article 22 ensures that any person arrested must be informed of the grounds of arrest, allowed to consult and be defended by a lawyer, and produced before a magistrate within 24 hours. This right applies to both citizens and foreigners. However, enemy aliens and persons arrested under preventive detention laws are not entitled to this protection. The provision safeguards individual liberty against arbitrary state action. It also lays down safeguards for preventive detention laws through Articles 22(3) to 22(7).

question: Which of the following is a constitutional body in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Election Commission of India
NITI Aayog
National Human Rights Commission
Central Information Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Election Commission of India

Explanation:
The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution. It is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in the country. In contrast, NITI Aayog, National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), and Central Information Commission (CIC) are statutory bodies, as they are created by acts of Parliament. NITI Aayog was formed in 2015 by an executive resolution, NHRC was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, and CIC under the Right to Information Act, 2005. Constitutional bodies derive their power and authority from the Constitution itself, while statutory bodies are created by laws passed by the legislature. Understanding this distinction is crucial for competitive exams.

question: Which of the following Acts made the Governor-General of India the Viceroy of India? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Government of India Act, 1858
Government of India Act, 1935
Indian Councils Act, 1909
Government of India Act, 1919
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1858

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1858 ended the rule of the East India Company and transferred the administration of India directly to the British Crown. Under this Act, the Governor-General was given the title of Viceroy, who acted as the representative of the British monarch. Lord Canning became the first Viceroy of India. The Act also created the position of the Secretary of State for India, who was a member of the British Cabinet.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस अधिनियम ने भारत के गवर्नर-जनरल को भारत का वायसराय बनाया? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1858
भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935
भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम, 1909
भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1919
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1858

Explanation:
भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1858 ने ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के शासन को समाप्त कर भारत का प्रशासन सीधे ब्रिटिश क्राउन को सौंप दिया। इस अधिनियम के तहत गवर्नर-जनरल को वायसराय की उपाधि दी गई, जो ब्रिटिश सम्राट का प्रतिनिधि बन गया। पहले वायसराय लॉर्ड कैनिंग थे। इस अधिनियम ने भारत सचिव का पद भी सृजित किया, जो ब्रिटिश कैबिनेट का सदस्य होता था।

question: Which of the following is true regarding the writ jurisdiction under Articles 32 and 226 of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: The writ of Quo Warranto can only be issued by the President of India.
Only the Supreme Court has the authority to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
Under Article 32, Parliament has the power to allow other courts to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
High Courts can issue writs under Article 226 only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Under Article 32, Parliament has the power to allow other courts to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights

Explanation:
Article 32 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. It also allows Parliament to authorise any other court to exercise the same power within its territorial jurisdiction. In contrast, Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs not only for Fundamental Rights but also for other legal rights. The writ of Quo Warranto is not issued by the President; it is a judicial remedy. The Supreme Court does not have exclusive authority to issue writs for Fundamental Rights; High Courts can also do so under Article 226. Thus, option 3 is correct.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which Article deals with Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction? → Article 32
☛ Which Article deals with High Court's writ jurisdiction? → Article 226
☛ What writs can be issued under Article 32? → Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto
☛ Can Parliament empower other courts to issue writs under Article 32? → Yes, by law
☛ Under Article 226, writs can be issued for which rights? → Both Fundamental and other legal rights
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 32 और 226 के अंतर्गत रिट अधिकार क्षेत्र के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सत्य है? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: परमादेश रिट केवल भारत के राष्ट्रपति द्वारा जारी की जा सकती है।
केवल उच्चतम न्यायालय को मौलिक अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन के लिए रिट जारी करने का अधिकार है।
अनुच्छेद 32 के अंतर्गत, संसद को अन्य न्यायालयों को मौलिक अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन के लिए रिट जारी करने की अनुमति देने का अधिकार है।
उच्च न्यायालय अनुच्छेद 226 के अंतर्गत केवल मौलिक अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन के लिए रिट जारी कर सकते हैं।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 32 के अंतर्गत, संसद को अन्य न्यायालयों को मौलिक अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन के लिए रिट जारी करने की अनुमति देने का अधिकार है

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 32 मौलिक अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन के लिए सर्वोच्च न्यायालय को रिट जारी करने का अधिकार देता है। साथ ही, यह अनुच्छेद संसद को यह शक्ति प्रदान करता है कि वह किसी अन्य न्यायालय को भी मौलिक अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन के लिए रिट जारी करने का अधिकार दे सकती है। अनुच्छेद 226 के तहत उच्च न्यायालय मौलिक अधिकारों के अलावा अन्य कानूनी अधिकारों के लिए भी रिट जारी कर सकते हैं। परमादेश रिट केवल राष्ट्रपति द्वारा नहीं, बल्कि न्यायालयों द्वारा जारी की जाती है। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के पास मौलिक अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन के लिए रिट जारी करने की एकमात्र शक्ति नहीं है; उच्च न्यायालय भी अनुच्छेद 226 के तहत ऐसा कर सकते हैं। इसलिए, विकल्प 3 सही है।

☛ अनुच्छेद 226 किसे संबोधित करता है? → उच्च न्यायालयों को

☛ क्या संसद अनुच्छेद 32 के तहत अन्य न्यायालयों को रिट शक्ति दे सकती है? → हाँ, विधि द्वारा
